_note: Machine-checkable form of the Deliverable Quality Bar in SKILL.md. Worksheet coverage, per-row fields and per-red counts are code; heuristics are checked against the skill's own examples, since a copied example is by construction not product-specific. All 19 bars are checked. Notes: red_rows_x3 repeats the red-row list three times so one metric-change line per alternative (A, B, C) can be counted against every 🔴 row; patterns_named is only a floor (a baseline also names infinite scroll or read receipts), the per-row semantic current_state_specific carries the real judgment; the per-red Business Tension and radical-alternative counts read the labelled lines the skill's Step 3 template produces.

semantic.bar: names specific exploitation patterns (infinite scroll, filter bubbles) rather than vague concerns
semantic.instructions: Does `items[{i}]` name at least one specific design mechanism of this product that exploits users, rather than only a vague concern?

criteria.true: Names a concrete mechanism or feature, such as infinite scroll, autoplay, streaks, read receipts, a hidden desirability score, personalized feed, blurred teaser profiles or push alerts, and says what it does.
criteria.false: Only a general worry such as 'users may feel bad', 'engagement is high' or 'the design is manipulative' with no named mechanism.

semantic.bar: explicitly addresses algorithmic-bias mechanisms when scoring/ranking/filtering is present
semantic.instructions: Does `items[0]` name at least one specific algorithmic-bias mechanism and say which group it disadvantages?

criteria.true: Names a mechanism such as engagement amplification of anxiety-provoking content, Elo-style scoring carrying historical participation bias, beauty-filter colorism, or a demographic proxy standing in for merit, AND names who it disadvantages.
criteria.false: Only says the algorithm 'might be biased' or 'should be audited' with no mechanism, or names a mechanism with no affected group.

semantic.bar: generates concrete alternatives with metric trade-offs and business tensions
semantic.instructions: Do the alternatives in `items[0]` each describe a specific change to a named feature, with an expected change in a named metric?

criteria.true: Alternatives name a concrete change to a named product feature (for example a 'load more' button after 10 items) and say which metric moves and in which direction.
criteria.false: Alternatives are general aspirations such as 'be less addictive' or 'improve wellbeing', or give no metric consequence.

semantic.bar: flags when measures of success themselves indicate exploitation
semantic.instructions: Does `items[0]` name the product's own success metric and say that the metric itself rewards extraction or conflicts with user wellbeing?

criteria.true: Names a specific metric (for example time spent, DAU, streak retention, paid conversion) and states that optimizing it works against users, so the metric is part of the problem.
criteria.false: Discusses harms of features only, or mentions metrics without saying the metric itself conflicts with wellbeing.
